_doc: M2.5: the ISO metric coarse thread and what hangs off it, for circuit boards and single-board computers. Holes, the socket cap, countersunk and hexagon heads, nuts, washer, set screw, the lengths sold and its strength, each from its standard as tabulated on the pages its source names; its heat-set insert (CNC Kitchen's) is a community figure until measured; its pilot in plastic is Bambu Lab's figure, community until measured. The names designs have always read keep their values: clearance is the ISO 273 normal hole, head and head_height the ISO 4762 socket cap head, nut_flats and nut_height the ISO 4032 nut. kind as in x1c.json.
name: m2_5

thread_form.rule: An ISO metric thread, coarse pitch (60° flanks)
thread_form.source: ISO 261 and ISO 262 (general purpose metric threads, coarse and fine pitches), as tabulated at https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_metric_screw_thread and in the thread column of https://www.fasteners.eu/standards/ISO/4762/

thread.rule: The thread as it is written: M2.5 is 2.5 mm across with a 0.45 mm pitch
thread.source: ISO 261 and ISO 262 (general purpose metric threads, coarse and fine pitches), as tabulated at https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_metric_screw_thread and in the thread column of https://www.fasteners.eu/standards/ISO/4762/

major_diameter.source: ISO 261 and ISO 262 (general purpose metric threads, coarse and fine pitches), as tabulated at https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_metric_screw_thread and in the thread column of https://www.fasteners.eu/standards/ISO/4762/

pitch.source: ISO 261 and ISO 262 (general purpose metric threads, coarse and fine pitches), as tabulated at https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_metric_screw_thread and in the thread column of https://www.fasteners.eu/standards/ISO/4762/

tap_drill.rule: Drill for tapping M2.5 coarse in metal: the major diameter less the pitch (some tables round it to 2.0)
tap_drill.source: ISO 2306 (drills for use before tapping), as tabulated at https://amesweb.info/Screws/metric-tap-drill-chart.aspx and https://www.engineeringtoolbox.com/metric-threads-d_777.html

clearance_close.rule: Clearance hole for an M2.5 screw, close fit (ISO 273 fine series)
clearance_close.source: ISO 273 (clearance holes for bolts and screws), as tabulated at https://www.amesweb.info/Screws/Metric-Clearance-Hole-Chart.aspx and in IS 1821:1987 (identical with ISO 273:1979) at https://law.resource.org/pub/in/bis/S01/is.1821.1987.pdf

clearance.rule: Clearance hole for an M2.5 screw, normal fit (ISO 273 medium series)
clearance.source: ISO 273 (clearance holes for bolts and screws), as tabulated at https://www.amesweb.info/Screws/Metric-Clearance-Hole-Chart.aspx and in IS 1821:1987 (identical with ISO 273:1979) at https://law.resource.org/pub/in/bis/S01/is.1821.1987.pdf

clearance_loose.rule: Clearance hole for an M2.5 screw, loose fit (ISO 273 coarse series)
clearance_loose.source: ISO 273 (clearance holes for bolts and screws), as tabulated at https://www.amesweb.info/Screws/Metric-Clearance-Hole-Chart.aspx and in IS 1821:1987 (identical with ISO 273:1979) at https://law.resource.org/pub/in/bis/S01/is.1821.1987.pdf

head.rule: M2.5 socket head cap screw head diameter, at most (dk max, plain head; a knurled head may be 4.68)
head.source: ISO 4762 (hexagon socket head cap screws), as tabulated at https://www.fasteners.eu/standards/ISO/4762/ and https://fasten.it/norms/norm/din_en_iso_4762 (DIN EN ISO 4762:2004-06)

head_height.rule: M2.5 socket head cap screw head height, at most (k max)
head_height.source: ISO 4762 (hexagon socket head cap screws), as tabulated at https://www.fasteners.eu/standards/ISO/4762/ and https://fasten.it/norms/norm/din_en_iso_4762 (DIN EN ISO 4762:2004-06)

head_key.rule: Hex key for an M2.5 socket head cap screw (s nominal)
head_key.source: ISO 4762 (hexagon socket head cap screws), as tabulated at https://www.fasteners.eu/standards/ISO/4762/ and https://fasten.it/norms/norm/din_en_iso_4762 (DIN EN ISO 4762:2004-06)

countersunk_head.rule: M2.5 countersunk socket screw head diameter where its cone would meet a sharp edge (dk theoretical max): a seat this wide takes any head flush. The head as made is at least 4.8. This size is in DIN EN ISO 10642:2020-02; the edition before it starts at M3
countersunk_head.source: ISO 10642 (hexagon socket countersunk head screws), as tabulated at https://fasten.it/norms/norm/din_en_iso_10642 (DIN EN ISO 10642:2020-02) and https://www.westfieldfasteners.co.uk/Standards/ScrewBolt_SHCsk_M.html

countersunk_head_height.rule: M2.5 countersunk socket screw head height, at most (k max): the depth of the cone from the sharp edge to the thread
countersunk_head_height.source: ISO 10642 (hexagon socket countersunk head screws), as tabulated at https://fasten.it/norms/norm/din_en_iso_10642 (DIN EN ISO 10642:2020-02) and https://www.westfieldfasteners.co.uk/Standards/ScrewBolt_SHCsk_M.html

countersunk_angle.rule: M2.5 countersunk head cone angle, across the whole cone (90° +2°)
countersunk_angle.source: ISO 10642 (hexagon socket countersunk head screws), as tabulated at https://fasten.it/norms/norm/din_en_iso_10642 (DIN EN ISO 10642:2020-02) and https://www.westfieldfasteners.co.uk/Standards/ScrewBolt_SHCsk_M.html

countersunk_key.rule: Hex key for an M2.5 countersunk socket screw (s nominal)
countersunk_key.source: ISO 10642 (hexagon socket countersunk head screws), as tabulated at https://fasten.it/norms/norm/din_en_iso_10642 (DIN EN ISO 10642:2020-02) and https://www.westfieldfasteners.co.uk/Standards/ScrewBolt_SHCsk_M.html

hex_head_flats.rule: M2.5 hexagon head screw width across flats (s nominal, the spanner size)
hex_head_flats.source: ISO 4017 (hexagon head screws, threaded to the head), as tabulated at https://www.fasteners.eu/standards/ISO/4017/ and https://fasten.it/norms/norm/din_en_iso_4017 (DIN EN ISO 4017:2014-10)

hex_head_height.rule: M2.5 hexagon head screw head height (k nominal)
hex_head_height.source: ISO 4017 (hexagon head screws, threaded to the head), as tabulated at https://www.fasteners.eu/standards/ISO/4017/ and https://fasten.it/norms/norm/din_en_iso_4017 (DIN EN ISO 4017:2014-10)

nut_flats.rule: M2.5 hexagon nut width across flats (s nominal)
nut_flats.source: ISO 4032 (hexagon regular nuts, style 1), as tabulated at https://www.fasteners.eu/standards/ISO/4032/ and https://fasten.it/norms/norm/din_en_iso_4032 (DIN EN ISO 4032:2013-04), and in the standard's own table 1 (ISO 4032:1999) at https://cdn.standards.iteh.ai/samples/26382/0f8d850e82f741f5b13e5ed78b236426/ISO-4032-1999.pdf

nut_height.rule: M2.5 hexagon nut height, at most (m max)
nut_height.source: ISO 4032 (hexagon regular nuts, style 1), as tabulated at https://www.fasteners.eu/standards/ISO/4032/ and https://fasten.it/norms/norm/din_en_iso_4032 (DIN EN ISO 4032:2013-04), and in the standard's own table 1 (ISO 4032:1999) at https://cdn.standards.iteh.ai/samples/26382/0f8d850e82f741f5b13e5ed78b236426/ISO-4032-1999.pdf

square_nut_flats.rule: M2.5 thin square nut width across flats (s nominal)
square_nut_flats.source: DIN 562 (square thin nuts), as tabulated at https://fasten.it/norms/norm/din_562 (DIN 562:2013-05) and https://www.fasteners.eu/standards/DIN/562/

square_nut_height.rule: M2.5 thin square nut height, at most (m max)
square_nut_height.source: DIN 562 (square thin nuts), as tabulated at https://fasten.it/norms/norm/din_562 (DIN 562:2013-05) and https://www.fasteners.eu/standards/DIN/562/

washer_bore.rule: M2.5 plain washer hole (d1 nominal, its least)
washer_bore.source: ISO 7089 (plain washers, normal series, product grade A), as tabulated at https://www.fasteners.eu/standards/ISO/7089/ and https://fasten.it/norms/norm/din_en_iso_7089

washer_diameter.rule: M2.5 plain washer outside diameter (d2 nominal, its most)
washer_diameter.source: ISO 7089 (plain washers, normal series, product grade A), as tabulated at https://www.fasteners.eu/standards/ISO/7089/ and https://fasten.it/norms/norm/din_en_iso_7089

washer_thickness.source: ISO 7089 (plain washers, normal series, product grade A), as tabulated at https://www.fasteners.eu/standards/ISO/7089/ and https://fasten.it/norms/norm/din_en_iso_7089

set_screw_key.rule: Hex key for an M2.5 socket set screw (s nominal)
set_screw_key.source: ISO 4026 (hexagon socket set screws with flat point), as tabulated at https://www.fasteners.eu/standards/ISO/4026/ and https://fasten.it/norms/norm/din_en_iso_4026 (DIN EN ISO 4026:2004-05)

set_screw_point.rule: M2.5 flat point set screw: the diameter of its end, at most (dp max)
set_screw_point.source: ISO 4026 (hexagon socket set screws with flat point), as tabulated at https://www.fasteners.eu/standards/ISO/4026/ and https://fasten.it/norms/norm/din_en_iso_4026 (DIN EN ISO 4026:2004-05)

lengths.rule: The lengths an M2.5 socket head cap screw is sold in, from under the head. Longer ones are made but lie outside the standard's range for this thread, and the 18 and 75 mm some catalogues list are not ISO lengths
lengths.source: ISO 4762 nominal lengths, as tabulated at https://www.fasteners.eu/standards/ISO/4762/, within the range listed as commercial for this thread at https://fasten.it/norms/norm/din_en_iso_4762

property_class.rule: The steel property class the strength figure is for: 8.8, the lowest of the classes ISO 4762 screws are made in (8.8, 10.9, 12.9). Under M3 the standard leaves the class to agreement, so read the box an M2.5 screw came in. A 10.9 screw's proof stress is 830 MPa and a 12.9 screw's 970
property_class.source: ISO 898-1 (mechanical properties of steel fasteners), as tabulated by Bossard (01-2025) at https://www.bossard.com/ie-en/knowledge-hub/resources/technical-information/screws-property-class-04-to-12/ and, as JIS B 1051, at https://www.mikipulley.co.jp/en/resources/standards-steel-bolts-screws; proof loads at https://www.engineeringtoolbox.com/metric-bolts-minimum-ultimate-tensile-proof-loads-d_2026.html; the classes ISO 4762 screws are made in as reproduced at https://www.boltport.com.ferrobend.com/standards/IS-2269

proof_stress.rule: Stress under proof load of a class 8.8 steel screw up to M16 (Sp): what an M2.5 screw holds with no permanent set. Its tensile strength is 800 MPa
proof_stress.source: ISO 898-1 (mechanical properties of steel fasteners), as tabulated by Bossard (01-2025) at https://www.bossard.com/ie-en/knowledge-hub/resources/technical-information/screws-property-class-04-to-12/ and, as JIS B 1051, at https://www.mikipulley.co.jp/en/resources/standards-steel-bolts-screws; proof loads at https://www.engineeringtoolbox.com/metric-bolts-minimum-ultimate-tensile-proof-loads-d_2026.html; the classes ISO 4762 screws are made in as reproduced at https://www.boltport.com.ferrobend.com/standards/IS-2269

stainless_class.rule: The stainless grade and class the second strength figure is for: A2-70, austenitic steel, cold worked, the class ISO 4762 names for stainless screws up to M20
stainless_class.source: ISO 3506-1 (mechanical properties of stainless steel fasteners), as tabulated by Bossard (01-2025) at https://www.bossard.com/ie-en/knowledge-hub/resources/technical-information/stainless-steel-fasteners/: the one page read for the figure; the class from ISO 4762:1989 table 2, https://cdn.standards.iteh.ai/samples/10750/9750e048db9946af8360e67adb8cf0f9/ISO-4762-1989.pdf

stainless_proof_stress.rule: 0.2 % proof stress of an A2-70 stainless screw (Rp0.2), at least. Its tensile strength is 700 MPa at least
stainless_proof_stress.source: ISO 3506-1 (mechanical properties of stainless steel fasteners), as tabulated by Bossard (01-2025) at https://www.bossard.com/ie-en/knowledge-hub/resources/technical-information/stainless-steel-fasteners/: the one page read for the figure; the class from ISO 4762:1989 table 2, https://cdn.standards.iteh.ai/samples/10750/9750e048db9946af8360e67adb8cf0f9/ISO-4762-1989.pdf

insert_diameter.rule: CNC Kitchen M2.5 x 4 heat-set insert: its diameter over the knurls (D1)
insert_diameter.source: CNC Kitchen, heat-set insert dimensions and design guidelines (the maker's own sheet), https://www.cnckitchen.com/s/CNCKitchen_Heat-Set-Insert-Dimensions-and-Design-Guidelines.pdf, with its guide page https://www.cnckitchen.com/blog/tipps-amp-tricks-fr-gewindeeinstze-im-3d-druck-3awey

insert_length.rule: CNC Kitchen M2.5 x 4 heat-set insert length (L)
insert_length.source: CNC Kitchen, heat-set insert dimensions and design guidelines (the maker's own sheet), https://www.cnckitchen.com/s/CNCKitchen_Heat-Set-Insert-Dimensions-and-Design-Guidelines.pdf, with its guide page https://www.cnckitchen.com/blog/tipps-amp-tricks-fr-gewindeeinstze-im-3d-druck-3awey

insert_hole.rule: Printed hole for a CNC Kitchen M2.5 x 4 heat-set insert (D2), straight, not tapered. Already sized for printing: no hole compensation. The maker says to test it on your printer, since holes print small
insert_hole.source: CNC Kitchen, heat-set insert dimensions and design guidelines (the maker's own sheet), https://www.cnckitchen.com/s/CNCKitchen_Heat-Set-Insert-Dimensions-and-Design-Guidelines.pdf, with its guide page https://www.cnckitchen.com/blog/tipps-amp-tricks-fr-gewindeeinstze-im-3d-druck-3awey

insert_depth.rule: Least depth of a blind hole for a CNC Kitchen M2.5 x 4 insert: its length and 1 mm. A through hole need be no longer than the insert
insert_depth.source: CNC Kitchen, heat-set insert dimensions and design guidelines (the maker's own sheet), https://www.cnckitchen.com/s/CNCKitchen_Heat-Set-Insert-Dimensions-and-Design-Guidelines.pdf, with its guide page https://www.cnckitchen.com/blog/tipps-amp-tricks-fr-gewindeeinstze-im-3d-druck-3awey

insert_wall.rule: Least wall of plastic round the hole of a CNC Kitchen M2.5 x 4 insert (W)
insert_wall.source: CNC Kitchen, heat-set insert dimensions and design guidelines (the maker's own sheet), https://www.cnckitchen.com/s/CNCKitchen_Heat-Set-Insert-Dimensions-and-Design-Guidelines.pdf, with its guide page https://www.cnckitchen.com/blog/tipps-amp-tricks-fr-gewindeeinstze-im-3d-druck-3awey

pilot.rule: Hole to draw for an M2.5 machine screw to form its own thread in printed PLA, the hole upright on the bed: Bambu Lab's figure for its own printers, as drawn, no hole compensation. Lying on its side the same hole is drawn 2.3. A starting figure: a printer's measured one comes first
pilot.source: Bambu Lab (MakerWorld official account), How to design screw holes for 3D printing, https://forum.bambulab.com/t/how-to-design-screw-holes-for-3d-printing/217352

pilot_depth.rule: Length of thread an M2.5 machine screw should engage in printed plastic, as Bambu Lab gives it
pilot_depth.source: Bambu Lab (MakerWorld official account), How to design screw holes for 3D printing, https://forum.bambulab.com/t/how-to-design-screw-holes-for-3d-printing/217352
